issue:
# Slide ID assignment fails when maximum slide ID is reached

## Description

I've encountered an issue with slide ID assignment when working with presentations that have slides with very large ID values.

The problem occurs in the `_next_id` property of the `CT_SlideIdList` class. When a presentation contains a slide with an ID at or near the maximum value (2147483647), the system fails to properly assign new slide IDs for additional slides.

## To Reproduce

Here's a simple script that demonstrates the issue:

```python
from pptx import Presentation

# Create a presentation with a slide that has a very large ID
# (This would normally be done by manipulating the XML directly)
prs = Presentation()
slide_list = prs.slides._sldIdLst

# Manually add a slide with maximum ID
# In real scenarios, this could happen when importing slides from other presentations
slide_list._add_sldId(id=2147483647, rId='rId2')

# Now try to add a new slide - this will fail to assign a proper ID
new_slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
print(f"New slide ID: {new_slide.slide_id}")
```

## Expected Behavior

When a presentation contains slides with IDs at or near the maximum value (2147483647), the system should still be able to assign valid IDs for new slides by finding the next available ID starting from the minimum valid ID (256).

## Actual Behavior

When trying to add a new slide to a presentation that already has a slide with ID 2147483647, the system fails to properly assign a new valid ID. Instead of falling back to finding an unused ID starting from 256, it attempts to use an ID greater than the maximum, which causes issues.

This is particularly problematic when working with presentations that have had slides added and removed multiple times, potentially leaving gaps in the ID sequence while also having some very high ID values.
